lines.text: Morning.
Mind the cart.
Two coppers for a turnip. Two!
Bread's up again. It's always up.
Rain by evening, my knee says.
You're not from the Waystation.
Another one off the road. They keep coming.
Don't stand in the well-queue unless you're drawing.
Is that blood? Don't tell me.
Chid rang the bell twice this morning. Nobody knows why.
The Flagon's ale is mostly water. The water's mostly ale.
Evening. Get indoors soon.
Nothing good walks about after dark.
Lamps are lit. Stay where they reach.
Is that the watch? Oh. You.
Shit weather, shit road, shit luck. Morning.
Bloody wolves. Bloody Watch. Bloody bread.
Holloway couldn't find his own arse with a lantern and a map.
Pell counts his coin in bed. Alone, obviously.
If the wolves don't get you, Rook's stew will.
My husband went out to the Verge a month back. Some days I hope he stays out.
Sella took three coppers off me for a smile. Worth four.
Rook's upstairs rooms go by the hour now. Don't ask how I know.
Somebody's having a better night than me. Rook's walls are thin.
Buried two this week. The ground's full and the priest's a boy.
They found the Aldo lad in the ditch. What was left of him.
Keep walking, hero. I've had my fill of heroes.
You smell like the dead. No offence. Everybody does, lately.
Came up the Low Ford at night? You're brave or daft.
They say the Ford-Warden's down. Was that you?
My gran swore the Warden was a story to keep children off the ford.
Wolves took the Oswin goats. In daylight!
Holloway's paying five a pelt, if you've the stomach.
Wolves don't behave like that. Not healthy ones.
Wolves at the gate last night. At the gate!
Tam's farm was hit. Poor lad's sleeping in the Watch-house.
You're the one who cleared the wolves. My boy can walk to the mill again.
Quiet out east now. Too quiet, Maeca says.
They say wolves walk beside you out there. I'd not believe it but for Maeca's face.
Wolf-friend. Keep them out of my hen-house, that's all I ask.
Tam says the stream runs clear again. Tam says a lot, but still.
Wenna's been smiling. Wenna. Smiling.
Pell's diggers moved their pipe. Pell, doing a kindness. Hm.
Heard somebody sold the Dig to Pell. Heard it was you.
You lied to Holloway about the wolves. Everybody knows. He does too.
Harlan's not slept since the wagons went.
The Coyle wagons had the Aldo boy's wedding cloth on them.
Kerchiefs, they say. Red rags and no mercy.
Jory Coyle's home! Harlan wept in the street, I saw it.
Those poor teamsters. Harlan hasn't opened the shutters.
Pell Varrow, selling his own neighbours. I bought eggs from that man.
Pell's been generous lately. With you, mostly.
Kerchiefs hit the Aldo farm again. Prices'll climb, you watch.
Salt's doubled. The Kerchiefs are bleeding the road dry.
The Roost burned, they say. You could see the smoke from the wall.
Redcowl dead. I'll believe it when I see the hat.
You made a deal with Redcowl? With Redcowl?
That's Coyle cloth on your back, isn't it.
Harlan says you brought every crate home. Every one.
Wanted, they said at the Watch. Wanted! You've a nerve walking here.
Did you feel the ground go, last night? Like something rolling over.
The shrine lamp's lit. First time since I was a girl.
Vonnra read your fortune? She never reads for free.
Chid says you died. You look well on it.
They carried you in past my door. I thought that was you done.
Are you a knight?
Tag! You're it!
Mum says not to talk to you.
Show us your sword! Go on!
Did you kill a wolf? A big one?
Is it true you've got a wolf for a friend?
All quiet. Keep it that way.
Gates are shut till dawn.
Walk on, traveller.
Piss off home. It's past curfew.
Keep that blade sheathed or I'll sheathe it for you.
Captain's doubled the gate. Wolves.
